scope: Port Qualcomm cpu-cluster cooling devices (qti_cpufreq_cdev) to native 7.3 cpufreq/freq-QoS/cpuhp/thermal; private cpufreq driver with phone tables only
factory_defects_found_by_review: Global list entries are devm memory but never removed: after remove/rebind, list walk and hotplug callback touch freed memory
reg_work not cancelled on remove (UAF if pending)
Concurrent online events can run registration twice: double freq_qos_add_request
Policy reference held until remove: cpufreq driver unregister waits forever in cpufreq_policy_put_kobj
Table built by raw index assuming no invalid holes and trusting sorted flag; freq_qos_add_request result ignored
regressions_before: First QEMU run: 4/9 because the test indexed clusters by array position; fdtoverlay reverses child order. Test now selects clusters by type name (as the HAL does); driver unchanged.
implemented: Per-device context with counted cluster array; multi-instance cpuhp state shared by refcount
Lifecycle mutex separate from callback state mutex (thermal register/unregister call ops)
CPUFREQ_CREATE_POLICY re-registers; CPUFREQ_REMOVE_POLICY drops cdev/QoS/policy ref synchronously
Valid entries (boost included, factory semantics) sorted descending and de-duplicated
verified: 9 KUnit cases on 4-CPU QEMU: phone tables -> cpu-cluster0 max 23 / cpu-cluster1 max 24 incl. 4 boost; ceilings 2611200 and 384000 kHz; release restores prior aggregate
Consumer before cpufreq driver registers on CREATE_POLICY
cpufreq driver unregister/re-register 3x completes and recovers
CPU2/3 offline/online keeps cdev and ceiling
40 duplicate online events: single registration, no WARN
Consumer rebind 3x; unsorted/invalid/duplicate table; no matching CPU rejected
Saved DT: cluster0=CPUs0-5, cluster1=CPUs6-7, no kernel cooling-map refs; phone sysfs max_state 23/24 equals table sizes
limits: SCMI cpufreq enforcement on hardware and thermal HAL use unverified
Whole-board boot, remaining drivers/DT/vendor_boot/dtbo/DLKM/SELinux and daily use remain
